The analysis's findings demonstrate that ML-based medical diagnostic systems are superior to conventional techniques in a number of ways, including increased accuracy, quicker diagnosis times, and reduced costs.The study also compares the system's performance with conventional medical diagnosis techniques and assesses its effectiveness based on a number of criteria. According to the study, ML-based medical diagnosis systems provide a number of important benefits over conventional techniques, including improved early-stage cancer detection and more precise prognosis prediction. In conclusion, the research findings and their consequences are discussed, future directions for research are suggested, and the study's limitations are emphasized. Overall, this work offers insightful information on the possibilities of machine learning for medical diagnostics and establishes a foundation for future investigations.

articleTitle: Leveraging Pre-trained Deep Learning Models for Orange Leaf Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: The research work investigates the use of pre-trained deep learning models, VGG16 and EfficientNetB3, for multi-class classification of orange leaf diseases. The paper aims at improving the accuracy and efficiency of disease diagnosis in orange crops which is also a contribution to the development of agricultural diagnostic tools. Using intensive data preprocessing, model adaptation, and fine-tuning, the research shows the models' ability to detect five specific disease classes as well as a healthy leaf. The VGG16 model achieved an overall accuracy of 89.5%, whereas the EfficientNetB3 model exceeded this with an accuracy of 92.3%, which demonstrates that the latter is better at capturing disease patterns with an optimally balanced network. The findings demonstrate that pre-trained models can be used in plant pathology and provide avenues for new research in agricultural technology. Through the strengths of VGG16 and EfficientNetB3, this study underlines the great advantages of deep learning models in disease detection procedures to promote sustainable and productive agricultural practices.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Deep Anomaly Detection Techniques- An Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: The area of anomaly identification in images, using deep learning techniques, has garnered considerable interest in recent years owing to its extensive applicability across many fields. Anomaly Detection also referred to as outlier identification, aims to find data instances that display substantial deviations from the rest of the existing data. This paper provides a thorough analysis of prior research that has suggested approaches for identifying abnormalities in images and videos through the use of deep learning technologies. This paper emphasizes on a more detailed perspective of the differences in research efforts by examining factors such as the methods used for anomaly detection, the datasets used, the evaluation metrics used, and the approach used to get deep anomaly detection results. It concludes by discussing the difficulties and possible directions for future research on the detection of abnormalities.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband High Gain Full Active Bias LNA With Improved Noise Figure for OTH Radar’s Receiver Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: This paper introduces a High Frequency (HF) band, Continuous Wave (CW), High Gain, Broadband Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) implemented using silicon-based Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT) technology on a single board. This LNA will be used in the receiver section of an Over The Horizon (OTH) Radar and is capable of working in the entire HF band i.e. from 3 MHz to 30 MHz. Class-A configuration of amplifier design is been used here with a completely Active Biasing technique. A gain of more than 28 dB for a single stage is been achieved and the noise figure (NF) of the circuit is less than 2.5 dB in the entire range of operation. Also a mathematical analysis has been done to showcase the improvement in noise figure. This novel design is not only limited to OTH Radar but also can be used for Amateur Radio Communication and Ionosonde Experiments purpose.

articleTitle: Integrating Electric Vehicle Loads into IEEE 33-Bus System: An Analysis on the Role of DSTATCOM in Maintaining System stability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Electric Vehicle (EV) integration into the power grid, specifically within the IEEE 33-bus system, brings significant challenges in terms of voltage stability and power losses. This study examines the impact of various EV models - OLA S1 Pro, Air, X+, and X - and proposes using Distribution Static Synchronous Compensators (DSTATCOM) for mitigation. Utilizing the Voltage Stability Index (VSI) for optimal EV load placement and Power Loss Index (PLI) for DSTATCOM positioning, the study reveals that while EVs increase line losses and voltage instability, DSTATCOM deployment effectively counters these issues, enhancing the system’s stability.

articleTitle: Analyzing 5kW Rooftop Residential Photovoltaic System using System Advisor Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Renewable energy sources offer a promising future, harnessing the power of nature, clean and pure. These resources provide abundant energy from the Sun rays and the Wind formulation. Nowadays, for reducing carbon footprint and pollution, these are the promising sources to cater for the load demand. The System Advisor Model (SAM) is a software tool developed by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL). SAM simulates and evaluates the efficiency and profitability of different renewable energy systems, such as solar photovoltaic, wind energy, biogas, geothermal, etc. This research paper represents the overview of the performance model of a 5kW residential PV system, which demonstrates the annual energy generated, capacity factor, levelized cost of energy (LCoE), degradation in energy generation, etc. A case for the residential owner of the solar PV system is considered for the work with a low base and high load demand. The computation of power-sharing by the solar PV system and grid is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Automated Quantification of Mammographic Density in Craniocaudal Oblique-View Radiographs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Breast density plays a pivotal role in assessing breast cancer risk, influencing both the likelihood of developing the disease and the potential for radiologists to miss small lesions in mammograms. Therefore, reliable and automated methods for analysing breast tissue density are essential for radiologists. In this study, we propose a U-Net neural network trained on 170 craniocaudal oblique-viewed mammograms to identify breast tissue. The trained model is then employed to segment breast tissue and estimate surface density using the pixel count method. Our results demonstrate high accuracy for both breast area segmentation (98%) and breast tissue segmentation (97%), with IoU scores of 0.93 and 0.83, respectively. Moreover, we compare our technique to existing state-of-the-art methods and confirm its superior performance.

articleTitle: Effect of ESR on the bifurcation of Valley V2-modulated Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: In this paper, valley-V2 modulation method is implemented in a buck converter. Valley-V2 modulation is a ripple-based fixed frequency modulation method where the valley (minimum or lowest) value of output ripple voltage is used for modulation. Discreet mathematical model has been developed for the converter. We explore the nonlinear dynamical behavior of the said system with the help of bifurcation diagram. ESR(effective series resistance) value of a filter capacitor is very important parameter in a ripple-based controller. Here, we have done an intensive study of how the dynamics of the converter are influenced by the ESR. We explore that how the value of ESR dominates the nature of bifurcation as well as stability of the system.

articleTitle: Multi-board Synchronization of n-channel Direct RF Digital Transceiver for Active Phased Array Radar using JESD204 Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Achieving synchronization in multi-channel transmit and receive systems has traditionally involved complex length-matched channel designs, posing challenges, particularly in higher-order channels. This paper introduces an innovative approach to multi-board synchronization of n-channel direct RF digital transceivers utilizing the high-speed serial JESD204 protocol, which leverages RF PLLs, high-speed serial DACs, and ADCs. The synchronization technique discussed herein significantly impacts digital beamforming (DBF) in active phased array RADAR systems. Instead of relying on a matched device clock or SYSREF signal, the proposed method employs phase delay calculation and PLL reprogramming to adjust phase differences among channels.Synchronization is accomplished through online phase delay calculation within the FPGA using cross-correlation techniques between channels. Notably, this approach eliminates the need for a matched device clock or SYSREF signal, thereby reducing PCB complexity. Results underscore the method's efficacy, making it an efficient solution for active phased array RADAR systems, while a new method has been explored to analyze the impact of random phase changes on digital beamforming.

articleTitle: RoboPaint-The proposed Wall Painting Robot: A Unified Control System Integrating Hardware and Software for Efficient Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: It is vital to note that the demand for painters in the construction industry is currently high and expected to continue increasing in developed and developing countries shortly. However, relying on manual labor for construction tasks is costly, time-consuming, and less precise and hazardous to workers' health. The solution to these challenges lies in embracing automation, leveraging advanced technologies like computer vision and path projection to guide robotic systems in completing tasks with greater efficiency and accuracy. By adopting this approach, we can not only enhance productivity but also ensure the safety and wellbeing of workers in the construction sector. The Algorithm presented in this context is exceptional and offers several advantages over existing literature. The detailed dynamic model parameters further enhance the robot's features, making it a significant breakthrough in the construction industry.

articleTitle: Leveraging Parameter Efficient Training Methods for Low Resource Text Classification: A case study in Marathi
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: With the surge in digital content in low-resource languages, there is an escalating demand for advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques tailored to these languages. BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers), serving as the foundational framework for numerous NLP architectures and language models, is increasingly employed for the development of low-resource NLP models. Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) is a method for fine tuning Large Language Models (LLMs) and reducing the training parameters to some extent to decrease the computational costs needed for training the model and achieve results comparable to a fully fine-tuned model. In this work, we present a study of PEFT methods for the Indic low-resource language Marathi. We conduct a comprehensive analysis of PEFT methods applied to various monolingual and multilingual Marathi BERT models. These approaches are evaluated on prominent text classification datasets like MahaSent, MahaHate, and MahaNews. The incorporation of PEFT techniques is demonstrated to significantly expedite the training speed of the models, addressing a critical aspect of model development and deployment. In this study, we explore Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models (LoRA) and adapter methods for low-resource text classification. We show that these methods are competitive with full fine-tuning and can be used without loss in accuracy. This study contributes valuable insights into the effectiveness of Marathi BERT models, offering a foundation for the continued advancement of NLP capabilities in Marathi and similar Indic languages.

Author Keywords: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

articleTitle: LAWBOT: A Smart User Indian Legal Chatbot using Machine Learning Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Legal documents and articles in India are abound on the Internet and in libraries, making it a tedious task for the average person unfamiliar with the legal field to wade through. They need proper guidance, be it filling out forms, understanding legal terms of service, filing a complaint, or any other legal activity. Developing a simple and efficient chatbot that utilizes the complex dataset and uses natural language processing to provide information about applicable laws and documents is essential. We propose Machine Learning framework based LAWBOT which aims to create a conversational chatbot for these users to easily ask legal questions, find lawyers, and review lawsuit documents.

articleTitle: Blockchain and Deep Learning for Agricultural Advancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: The agriculture sector plays a significant role as it not only serves in meeting a substantial portion of worldwide food requirements but is also servers as one of the key contributors to the country’s economy. However, some issues including economic inequality, unpredictability of weather patterns, and crop diseases seek for a solution which offers enhanced crop traceability and insurance automation to address food safety problems and financial difficulty. This study creates a prototype of a crop management system merging blockchain and deep learning technologies, assessing its practical aspects. Blockchain enhances data storage, traceability, and transparency, while deep learning boosts monitoring, disease detection, and crop recommendation. The proposed work demonstrates the system’s advantages and hurdles thereby contributing to a more efficient and transparent crop management paradigm which aims to revolutionize the crop management system by adopting sustainable agricultural practices on a globally.

articleTitle: Conventional CMOS technology based RadFET dosimeter for Ionizing Radiation Detection for High Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: In CMOS integrated circuits (ICs), major failures can be caused by the electrical breakdown in the region of oxides and interfaces when the CMOS ICs are subjected conditions like space environment or high energy laboratory settings. When it comes to addressing radiation impacts and preventing circuit failures, the utilization of Triple Modular Redundancy (TMR) and the radiation harden shielding at both the circuit level and/or system levels is beneficial. On the other hand, this strategy may incur additional costs and bring additional strain on the system. RADFETs are widely employed dosimeters that have found considerable application in space and particle accelerator environments. This work proposes an optimized radiation sensor for detecting and measuring radiation effects. The primary goal of this proposed work is to develop a radiation sensor capable of accurately detecting and measuring radiation doses with precision. The mathematical and modeling findings that are used to determine the oxide thickness of the sensor. Other parameters are adopted from SCL 180 nm CMOS technology. The simulation of a RadFET dosimeter is accomplished through the use of the Cogenda TCAD simulator. The substrate material used is Silicon with a Na doping concentration of 1e16 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> and 300 nm is an oxide thickness of the RaDFET dosimeter. The simulated threshold voltage is -0.9 V, whereas the calculated threshold voltage is -0.96 V. For testing purposes, the sensor underwent radiation dose exposure from 10 krad to 200 krad TID dose. Threshold voltage shift is adopted as a sensitivity parameter. The sensor exhibits a sensitivity of 89 μV/rad within the range of 0 to 100 krad and 10 μV/rad for 100 krad to 200 krad range

articleTitle: Analysis of Web Application Vulnerabilities using Dynamic Application Security Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: In the era of ubiquitous digital connectivity, securing software applications against cyber threats is paramount. Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST) has emerged as a crucial methodology in the realm of cybersecurity, providing a dynamic, real-time approach to identify and mitigate vulnerabilities within software applications. This research paper delves into the significance and application of DAST in fortifying cybersecurity measures. DAST represents a departure from traditional static testing methods, which analyze source code or binaries, by assessing applications during runtime. The methodology involves the active, controlled probing of live applications through simulated cyber-attacks, including injection of malicious payloads and emulation of common exploit techniques. By dynamically assessing how applications respond to these simulated threats, DAST offers a real-world evaluation of security posture, facilitating the identification of potential vulnerabilities.This research paper analyzed the Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST) reports for different web applications over the past two years and provide a valuable resource for cybersecurity practitioners, researchers, and organizations striving to adopt effective strategies in safeguarding their digital assets against evolving cyber threats in the current environment.

articleTitle: Optimizing Lithium-Ion Battery Performance in Electric Vehicles: A Comprehensive Analysis of Temperature, Humidity, and Moisture Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are crucial for electric vehicles (EVs) due to their high energy density and extended lifespan. However, their performance is significantly influenced by temperature, humidity, and moisture. This paper investigates the impact of high and low temperatures, humidity, and moisture on lithium-ion batteries for EV applications. Additionally, the study explores the effects of external factors such as air quality, dust, particles, and solar radiation. The paper investigates the occurrence of thermal runaway, provides insights into state-of-charge (SOC) estimation methods employed by leading EV manufacturers, and proposes strategies to overcome temperature-related challenges. Additionally, the paper presents the results of developed simulation models that demonstrate the influence of temperature on battery performance. Finally, the paper discusses the challenges and opportunities associated with mitigating the impact of these environmental factors on EV batteries.

articleTitle: Crowded Massive MIMO Systems: A Random-Access Protocol forPilot Allocation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: To control the explosive expansion of wireless data traffic, a large multiple-input multiple was used. The spatial multiplexing of many tens of user equipments (UEs) allows massive MIMO to attain incredible spectral efficiency. These improvements can only be realized in real life if many more UEs than currently exist can connect to the network in an effective manner. The randomaccess mechanism is crucial to distributing the finite number of pilots across the UEs when the number of UEs rises and each UE only sometimes enters the network. We explore the random access problem in the context of Massive MIMO in this research and create a redesigned protocol called Strongest-User Collision Resolution (SUCRe). With the chance that other UEs will also submit the same pilot, an accessing UE requests a dedicated pilot by sending an ad hoc random access pilot. With the help of distributed collision detection, which is made possible by the advantageous massive MIMO channel propagation, each UE can assess the strength of the competing signals and choose to repeat the pilot if it believes that its signal is the strongest at the receiver. Most issues are resolved with the SUCRe protocol. In dense metropolitan settings, the pilot collides, but continues to allow UEs effectively in congested networks.

articleTitle: On the Complexity Aspects of Various Sub-classes of Linear Languages
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: The non-terminals in the underlying grammar play an important role in determining different characteristics of the language generated. The languages generated by the grammars are determined by a unique non-terminal known as the start symbol. Even without altering any of the production rules, the grammar produces a distinct language if we swap the start symbol for any other non-terminal. Occasionally, we purposefully include extra non-terminals to attain specific characteristics in both the grammar and parse trees. One such scenario is when we convert a language to Chomsky’s Normal Form (CNF), in which case we add additional non-terminals to convert the parse tree into a binary tree. In this paper, we consider different sub classes of CFLs by restricting the number of nonterminals. We study different characteristics like the generative power of the grammar, the stack height, and the number of turns of the PDA which accept the languages produced by the grammars. We show that these characteristics are influenced by the number of nonterminals in the grammar.

articleTitle: Multiclass Classification of Tomato Leaf Diseases using a Hybrid of LSTM and CNN Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Identifying diseases on tomato leaves is very important as tomatoes contain a rich amount of vitamins and other essential compounds for the human body. It helps keep crops healthy and makes farming last longer. Tomato leaf diseases are big problems for farmers and the farming business. Some of the key challenges associated with tomato leaf diseases include: Plant diseases in the leaves of tomato plants directly lead to a decrease in crop production. Diseases like early blight, late blight and bacterial wilt cause leaves to fall off too soon. This results in the plant's ability to grow fruit properly. Diseases in leaves can affect tomatoes by decreasing fruit production with weird shapes and marks. This not only makes the food look bad but can also result in people saying no to buying it and making its worth lower. In the proposed work, we proposed a strong ensemble model that uses Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). This helps to accurately identify ten different types of tomato leaf diseases using a learning rate of 0.015, our hybrid model gets an accuracy at 99.8%. The model's performance is shown more by a loss value of 0.032, showing how good it is at finding complicated patterns in the data set. This smart method not only shows the strength of mixing LSTM and CNN designs, but it also helps in improving the classification accuracy of tomato leaf disease detection. It provides a trustworthy tool for farmers and scientists working on growing plants for many kinds of disease detection in tomato plants.

articleTitle: Eye Blink-based Morse Code Communication Tool for ALS Patient
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: The development of the Internet of Things(IoT) has boosted the inclusion and productivity of persons with impairments in modern society. This article discusses the challenges faced by individuals with speech and movement problems caused by motor neuron illnesses such as ALS and PLS, and the importance of technologies for augmented and alternative communication (AAC) in improving their quality of life. With 44% of India’s 2.68 billion specially challenged population having hearing, speech, or visual impairments, the need for cost-efficient and accessible AAC devices is significant. The article proposes a software solution that monitors eye blinks using OpenCV and Dlib libraries in Python, converting the blinking pattern into Morse code for universal communication. The software offers a simple and affordable alternative to existing AAC devices, enabling individuals with disabilities to interact with their environment and reduce their dependence on others.

articleTitle: Emulation of Nonlinear Dynamics of RF Power Amplifier on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: This paper presents a flexible field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-based emulation framework for RF power amplifiers (PAs). Emulation model of RF PA proves instrumental for testing their performance in hardware before manufacturing. It also facilitates faster design and optimization of advanced signal processing algorithms like digital predistortion. The applicability extends to broader use cases such as reconfigurable RF PAs. The proposed framework employs black-box modeling, obviating the need for internal constitution details and relying solely on input and output signal observations. The framework is built in MATLAB/Simulink® environment with HDL Coder tool box due to its parameterizability and flexibility in synthesizing hardware from a Simulink® design. The effectiveness of the proposed emulationframework is evaluated through FPGA emulation of GaN PA modules, namely, QPA2705 and GTRB424908FC/1 respectively on Xilinx Kintex-7® FPGA. Behavioral simulation results show that the performance of PA models having different non-linearity orders and memory depths matches well with that of PA output characterization data in terms of NMSE as well as ACEPR. The emulation model’s validation was performed through an in-depth analysis, encompassing power curves, as well as power spectral density plots. Various models were examined and compared based on their accuracy and hardware complexity. FPGA emulation results for PA are shown to be precisely matching with that of behavioral simulation. Besides, the paper also compares the resource utilization for FPGA synthesis of PA models.

articleTitle: Applying Machine Learning and the Gradient Boosting Classification Method for Evaluating the Probability of Autism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: This research investigates the use of machine learning, especially the Gradient Boosting Classification (GBC) technique, to evaluate the likelihood of autism. Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is an intricate neurodevelopmental illness that may range in severity, highlighting the need of promptly and accurately diagnosing the disorder to ensure successful management. Conventional diagnostic techniques depend on clinical assessments, which may be subjective and time-consuming. This study used a dataset that includes a wide range of demographic and clinical characteristics to train and fine-tune a Gradient Boosting Classification model. The GBC algorithm is selected because to its capacity to manage intricate connections within data, adjust to non-linear patterns, and provide exceptional forecast accuracy. The research showcases the efficacy of the GBC model in accurately categorising persons with and without autism, yielding encouraging outcomes in terms of sensitivity, specificity, and overall performance metrics. The results indicate and access that machine learning, namely the GBC technique, has the ability to enhance the effectiveness and impartiality of autism diagnosis. This may lead to early intervention methods and better outcomes for persons with autism. Additional investigation and verification are necessary to enhance the model's potential to be applied to a wide range of situations and to incorporate and its effective employment into medical practise. The suggested Gradient Boosting Classifier achieves an accuracy of 93 percent during classification.

articleTitle: Real-time 3D Map Generation and Analysis Using Multi-channel LiDAR Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Accurate 3D environment reconstruction or 3D mapping is used in many fields, including robotics, autonomous vehicles, and virtual reality. LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) technology has emerged as a powerful sensing modality for capturing detailed 3D information about the surrounding environment. LiDAR comes with multiple channels and different field-of-view. The higher the number of channels denser will be the point cloud data. In this paper, the 3D map of a long stretch inside the IIT Hyderabad campus is created using the Velodyne LiDAR having 16, 32, 64, and 128 channels and their analysis are done. The number of LiDAR channels determines the density and resolution of the acquired point cloud. Higher channel configurations generally result in denser point clouds with finer details. However, dense point clouds can be computationally expensive to process and may require more storage space. Selecting keyframes to construct the 3D map reduces the computational time per frame, and the 3D reconstruction is done in real-time, even with the denser point cloud of 128-channel LiDAR. Lower channel configurations give sparse point cloud data, which may lack distinct features necessary for reliable matching. This paper comprehensively analyzes the 3D map created using Velodyne LiDAR with 16, 32, 64, and 128 channels.

articleTitle: Enhancing Multimedia Security through Advanced Image Authentication and Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: With this flood of multimedia data, protecting it is an absolute necessity. This paper describes a complete method for securing images that combines encryption and watermarking. A technique of the sort suggested further prolongs picture encryption, by interweaving a Rubik's idea with advanced encryptions like those based on Triple DES and AES. As further, a brand new strong watermarking algorithm is displayed. In this way, a high degree of protection for the copyright and genuineness is hoped to be achieved. The proposed method has encouraging results ensuring harvested photographs 'accessibility, confidentiality and integrity.

articleTitle: Analytical and Practical Perspectives on Fault Identification of Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Despite being a widely adopted method, the short-time Fourier transform fails to identify fault characteristic frequencies (FCF) from rapidly changing vibration signals. The wavelet transform further has the underlying issues of energy leakage, long computation time, interference term, and border distortion. The Hilbert-Haung transform (HHT) analyzes the vibration signal using intrinsic mode functions (IMFs), which are acquired through empirical mode decomposition (EMD). However, decomposition may produce redundant and extraneous IMFs that hamper the result accuracy. Furthermore, the use of the Hilbert transform (HT) in HHT for demodulation intensifies computational complexity and introduces subjective error in the FCF calculation. In this paper, an accurate and efficient signal analysis approach based on EMD, Correlation Coefficient (CC), Teager-Kaiser Energy Operator (TKEO), and Spectral Analysis (SA) is proposed for the FCF identification of an induction motor. Significant and related EMD-based decomposed IMFs are segregated by CC to avoid computational complexity and irrelevant analysis. Moreover, the computation of the envelope by the TKEO only requires three consecutive measurements of the IMF signals, making the result almost instantaneous.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Arrhythmia Detection Using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: In this paper, we present a convolutional neural network-based deep learning model that can classify different classes of arrhythmia from an ECG dataset. The model is trained on the Shaoxing People’s Hospital dataset, which contains ECG records for more than 10,000 people. After analysis, an accuracy of 84% was achieved using the created deep CNN algorithm. Furthermore, performance comparisons of different models, including support vector machine (SVM), K-nearest neighbors (KNN), random forests (RF), and an ensemble model, have been presented.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving digital landscape network security and efficiency are important especially with the increasingly widespread network anomalies that can cause severe performance degradation. Using dataset, Data preprocessing is performed. which includes removing missing values and standardizing attributes. A comparative analysis is been done among the models to determine the finest among them. The algorithm taken for comparing is Isolation Forest and it is compared with Random Forest, Decision Tree, K-mean and Logistic Regression. And the metrics for the comparison are accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, training time and testing time.

articleTitle: Analysis of Behavioral Artifacts of Malware for its Detection using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Malware is created with the express purpose of causing damage to a computer system. Malware may be examined using either static or dynamic analysis techniques. These techniques allow for the precise extraction of unique patterns, which may then be used to identify malware in files. In this research, we propose a behaviorally based approach to identifying malware. Since new malware families and variations are constantly being found on the internet and dark web, they constitute a particularly severe danger. To undo the damage done by malware might be difficult because of the encryption methods it employs. Malware proliferation tracks with AI's rapid development. Because machine learning and deep learning may identify previously unknown risks, its potential use in identifying malware is receiving a lot of attention. This approach yields prediction algorithms that can analyze the actions of malware to unearth new variations and families. There are a total of 3540 rows describing features of corrupted files and 6999 describing properties of uncorrupted files in the dataset. To achieve this, I used the 98.19% accurate Random Forest machine learning method and the 96.77% accurate KKN machine learning algorithm.

articleTitle: Fuzzy PI Based Speed control of Sensorless Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Utilizing a sensorless control approach allows the elimination of mechanical position sensors from the gearbox, thereby reducing maintenance costs and enhancing system robustness. This article presents a sensorless control system for permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drives, utilizing a model reference adaptive system (MRAS) observer with switching proportional-integral (PI) control and incorporating fuzzy logic control (FLC). The key contributions of this research encompass the introduction of a voltage compensation approach relying on a disturbance observer to address voltage distortion issues in PMSM systems powered by voltage source inverters (VSI). Additionally, a dual closed-loop FLC is devised for speed and current control, enhancing speed regulation performance, and command voltage accuracy, and eliminating the need for manual adjustment of control parameters. Furthermore, a sensorless control strategy employing a switching PI control-based MRAS observer is proposed for stator resistance tracking. The MRAS observer, by employing different thresholds, selects the suitable PI adaptive mechanism based on the current error variable's amplitude, thereby enhancing resistance estimation accuracy and dynamic performance in sensorless control. Experimental results are presented to validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Highway Asset Tracking for Enhanced Maintenance and Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Highway asset management and tracking is a critical aspect of transportation infrastructure maintenance and planning. It is a visionary approach to Precise Road Asset Detection and Enumeration is an innovative solution leveraging cutting-edge computer vision and AI technologies to automate asset counting on roadways accurately. By eliminating manual processes, it enhances efficiency, provides real-time data, and empowers authorities with valuable insights for effective infrastructure planning and maintenance. By capturing 360 images of highway assets during construction or installation, transportation agencies can create a comprehensive database of visual records and even the normal images provide a detailed visual representation of the assets, including their condition, configuration, and surrounding environment. Using the deep learning techniques first the pre-processing techniques are applied and then fed to the deep learning algorithms. These deep learning algorithms evaluate the images and give accurate results for asset tracking. By comparing which algorithm is the best for tracking the highway assets such as white stripes, light poles, and traffic signs by utilizing data, technology, and best practices, agencies can make informed decisions, optimize resources, and ensure the long-term sustainability of their highway networks.

articleTitle: Employee Monitoring System using Face Recognition Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: This research paper introduces an innovative Employee Monitoring System that utilizes Face Recognition Techniques, addressing the changing landscape of remote work, particularly heightened by the global COVID-19 pandemic. Employing deep learning, specifically focusing on the ResNet50 architecture, and real-time image analysis, the system aims to redefine how organizations monitor and empower their remote workforce. The introduction establishes the transformative potential of the project, positioning it as a pioneering effort in the dynamic realm of modern work. Delving into the scope, the project surpasses conventional monitoring systems by incorporating Haar Cascade face detection technology, offering real-time insights into individual activities during remote work. The paper meticulously details technical intricacies, including data collection methodologies, preprocessing techniques, and the development of a user-friendly web application. This comprehensive approach vividly illustrates the system's capabilities and its potential to optimize various facets of remote work operations. The paper's organization ensures a logical progression, commencing with the conceptualization and context in the introduction, followed by an in-depth exploration of technical aspects within the scope. Gratitude expressed to the project's contributors underscores the collective effort, from the invaluable guidance of the academic advisor to the collaborative endeavors of the exceptional team. The project's success stands as a testament to the collaborative spirit, innovative thinking, and dedication of all involved, with anticipated positive impacts on enhancing employee monitoring processes in the evolving landscape of remote work.

articleTitle: IOT Enabled:Air Flow Controlled Pollination System in Vertical Farming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: The research paper focuses on air-controlled pollination which introduces an innovative approach to address the crop yield challenge and importance of pollination in vertical farming. By accurately manipulating air currents, this method replicates the natural process of wind pollination by predicting from the selected parameters. The study analyzes various parameters like air velocity and direction and synchronizes them with plant development stages. This ensures precise and efficient pollination within the vertical farm environment. The paper demonstrates the potential of this technology to revolutionize vertical farming practices by enhancing crop yields, promoting biodiversity, and contributing significantly to sustainability in agriculture. It not only provides a solution for a pressing challenge faced by vertical farmers but also represents a remarkable amalgamation of advanced technology and ecological principles, marking significant progress in sustainable agriculture.

articleTitle: Development of Collaborative Learning Management Systems for Higher Education in Oncology Using Deep Learning and Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: As the situation rose globally with the COVID-19 pandemic, the educational system structure reformation started immediately after the hit of the severe pandemic. Online classrooms are formed for schools and undergraduate colleges; however, in the case of medical educational institutions, the key problem raised is about giving laboratory and practical anatomy training. Hence, the proposed research is developed for the oncology branch students for brain tumor assessments. The proposed system can collaborate with blockchain learning management systems and deep learning applications so that the learners can perform online practical analysis of adult brain tumor structures. In this newly developed system named ‘Onco-CNN-Board,’ the trainer can assign the BRATS data-set brain images, and learners can perform the extraction of the brain tumor for further analysis. Also, the proposed system is tested and validated using U-Net and V-Net models, and comparative analysis reveals that the U-Net model outperforms. Hence, the proposed research is revolutionary in the era of virtual learning management.

articleTitle: ChatGPT in Cyber Onslaught and Fortification: Past, Present, and Future
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Contemporary conversational models of language like ChatGPT have progressed tremendously in recent years. The comprehensive review includes ChatGPT's history, uses, challenges, and possible future advancements. The paper review also comprises the role of ChatGPT in cyber onslaught and cyber fortification. ChatGPT has numerous benefits, but it also has certain drawbacks. Depending on the data it is trained on, one of its challenges may be bias. Lastly, because ChatGPT is still in its early stages of development, it occasionally struggles to comprehend complex or complex commands. This paper review tackle ChatGPT's and other generative AI models' futures in their concluding remarks. They forecast that ChatGPT will become continually integrated with other technologies, like augmented reality and virtual assistants. Furthermore, they predict that ChatGPT will become more and more important in domains like scientific research and others that need sophisticated natural language processing.

articleTitle: Elucidating the role of Device architecture for Mott-insulator based Memory technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Emerging memory technologies are driven by the escalating demand for advanced, high-performance, and energy-efficient memory solutions. Traditional technologies, while effective, face challenges in meeting the demands of modern computing and data storage applications. As the demand for enhanced data retrieval speed, reduced energy consumption, and greater scalability grows, emerging memory technologies like Magnetic Random-Access Memory (MRAM), Resistive Random-Access Memory (ReRAM), and Phase-Change Random Access Memory (PCRAM) are becoming increasingly prominent. ReRAM, distinguished by its unique resistive switching mechanism, facilitates reversible transitions between high and low-resistance states, providing a foundation for efficient data storage. A noteworthy aspect of ReRAM is the utilization of Mott insulators, such as VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, known for their remarkable insulator-to-metal transition (IMT) capabilities. This unique property allows ReRAM to achieve precise and energy-efficient control over resistance states, contributing to its allure as a promising alternative in the ever-evolving landscape of memory technologies.

articleTitle: ResNet-50 Powered Masked Face Detection: A Deep Learning Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Due to the widespread use of face masks as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, facial recognition technology, which is routinely employed for security screening in workplaces, is encountering substantial difficulties. These algorithms were commonly trained using photos of unmasked human faces, which posed challenges in recognising individuals wearing masks. In order to tackle this problem, this study introduces a deep learning model that is specifically tailored to properly identify individuals wearing masks. The model utilises the ResNet-50 architecture and has high proficiency in recognising individuals wearing face masks. The findings of this study can be incorporated into existing facial recognition software utilized for security screening purposes.

articleTitle: Energy Efficient Approaches for Routing Protocols in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN) play a crucial role in monitoring environmental conditions across diverse domains, including military operations, healthcare, agriculture, and disaster management. These networks consist of miniature wireless sensor nodes, each powered by a limited-lifespan battery. The key challenge in designing protocols and applications for WSN lies in ensuring longevity and dependability with a primary focus on energy consumption minimization and network lifetimeenhancement.This study aims to explore prevalent strategies of energy-efficient routing protocols to optimize node energy utilization. By delving into these protocols, we intend to uncover effective approaches that contribute to prolonging the life of WSNs.

articleTitle: Modeling of OWC System Employing Linear MMF
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Since optical wireless communication (OWC) can provide secure, affordable access solutions for wireless transmission while also relieving pressure on the extremely congested radio-frequency spectrum, it has become a substitute technology to radio communication. For the beyond 5G networks, hybrid OWC-multimode fiber (MMF) link is proposed to raise the time/frequency resource utilization. A 4×10Gbps OWC system employing linear MMF is modeled. Results depict that faithful MMF range of 400m is obtained with fixed 10km OWC range. Also, faithful OWC range of 90km is obtained with 100-200m fixed MMF range. A comparative performance indicates the superiority of the model w.r.t. existing ones.

articleTitle: Survey on Security Protocols for IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) represents a network of distinct objects with embedded software for exchanging transient states and data, essential for activating actuators. To interact with a cloud conducting big data analytics and supporting business decisions, edge networking devices and protocols are integral. Key sectors like industrial, agricultural, healthcare, and smart cities heavily rely on IoT, necessitating robust security measures. IoT protocols, functioning on IP protocols, address security across different layers, confronting challenges such as inconsistent manufacturing practices leaving hardware and data vulnerable. It is very significant to ensure data privacy, trust management, authentication and authorization in a heterogeneous environment. Addressing the vulnerabilities at edge and cloud service providers' sites are critical aspects to be addressed, which extensively details security breaches and the protective mechanisms offered by IoT protocols.

articleTitle: Intelligent Dictionary Elements Extraction using Optical Character Recognition and Deep Learning based Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: The Sanskrit Encyclopaedic Dictionary conceived and compiled by Deccan College Post Graduate Institute, Pune, India is available in paper format. For greater reach, there is a need for digitization of the dictionaries and conversion of these volumes into a comprehensive structured database. These volumes have Articles with a typical complex structure. In this paper, a novel approach for Automatic Lexical Element Extraction from Sanskrit Encyclopaedic Dictionary Pages (ALEE-SED) that consists of Sanskrit Dictionary Page Segmentation into articles and their meaning blocks using Optical Character Recognition (OCR) and Detectron2 Model further followed by an intelligent article wise dictionary (Lexical) element extraction is described.

articleTitle: Color Sorting Pick Up and Drop Robotic Arm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: The Color Sorting Pick-up and Drop Robotic Arm introduces a new automation system that is intended for efficient object handling in industrial settings. This system, which includes an RGB color sensor and accurate servo motors, combines sophisticated technology with intricate software controls. When taken as a whole, these components work to provide a thorough method for handling and organizing objects efficiently. By enabling the robotic arm to discern things based on their color attributes as detected by the color sensor, this study enhances colored item management and increases pick-and-place operations, precision and accuracy. Combining these technologies could lead to a large increase in productivity in businesses where accurate item sorting is essential. This research emphasizes how flexible and comprehensively these systems can be used to optimize many industrial processes, even outside of their immediate use. Developing a robotic arm that can be picked up and dropped in tandem with an automated color sorting system is the main goal of this research. This will validate the system’s implementation and open the door to further scalability and industrial automation-related application integration.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Detection Using integrated approach of FCM & CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: The diagnosis of brain tumors is a major issue in medical imaging, having the potential to have a large influence on patient outcomes. This abstract provides an overview of the obstacles, most recent breakthroughs, and ongoing research in brain tumor detection. Early diagnosis requires medical imaging modalities such as computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Previously, radiologists were evaluated manually, but with the emergence of deep learning algorithms, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), the field has experienced a revolution. When paired with large and diverse datasets, these AI-based algorithms have demonstrated promising results in automating the diagnosis of brain tumors, boosting accuracy, and reducing the workload for medical workers. However, there are still challenges, such as the need for larger datasets and the interpretability of AI models, even though CNN attained a very outstanding accuracy of 97.87% in our study. The fundamental purpose of this research is to distinguish between normal and abnormal pixels using statistical and texture-based criteria.

articleTitle: Impact of a Novel Convolution Neural Network on Chest X-Ray Images for Pneumonia Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Pneumonia is still considered as a major worldwide healthcare hazard which needs immediate treatment and timely and precise identification. The research paper shows the method for the precise identification of the disease with the use of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) on the Chest X-ray(CXR) images with the help of Batch normalisation, padding and data augmentation. The research uses a comprehensive dataset of 3450 CXR images. The experiments were conducted on over 200 epochs to ensure accuracy. Batch normalization and padding contributed to the stability and better interpretability of the CNN. Data Augmentation including Colour jitter made the training set more diverse for better generalization. The classification parameters like precision, recall ,F1 score and accuracy were used for the estimation of the model’s efficacy. The model showed a 96.02% accuracy reflecting its reliability in classification. This study gives medical professionals a dependable and effective tool that improves the state-of-the-art in pneumonia diagnosis.

articleTitle: Assistance to Uzbek people with speaking disabilities using Machine Learning and Sign Language Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: This paper presents an ongoing project addressing the communication needs of individuals with speaking disabilities, focusing on Uzbek sign language users. Leveraging machine learning, the application detects hand gestures in real-time, translating them into spoken Uzbek using Python, OpenCV, MediaPipe, and scikit-learn. Despite challenges in dataset creation, the Random Forest classifier achieves high accuracy. The current version demonstrates real-time hand gesture capture, accurate sign language recognition, and spoken translation. This work serves as a progress snapshot, with future plans to extend the application for real-time gesture recognition. The insights gained contribute to advancing assistive technologies, offering a promising solution for effective communication through sign language.

articleTitle: Estimation of Human Fall Detectionusing Body Pose Rule based Algorithm for Video Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Human fall detection is hot topic in the field of surveillance and health. The proposed approach consists of two parts: object detection with tracking and fall detection confirmation. The novelty of our work is that we have implemented algorithm which is composed of two rules for human fall detection. The outcomes of the algorithm demonstrate how correctly our model can identify the majority of single or multiple human falls quite accurately. The algorithm is performed on the publicly available benchmark UR Fall Detection datasetand analyzed using evaluation performance metrics. This paper aims to detect falls in a video stream using a combination of YOLOv3MobileNet model for human detection and AlphaPoseResNet model for detecting human poses and their keypoints.YOLOv3MobileNet pretrained model reduces the computational complexity and beneficial for real time fall detection. AlphaPoseResNet pretrained model having deeper backbone network offering high accuracy in pose estimation. One of the main challenges in fall detection systems is minimizing false positives while maintaining accurate fall detection. The proposed method shows that false alarms can be minimized while enhancing detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Temperature Dependent Coulomb Counting Method for State of Charge Estimation of Battery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: A battery’s State of Charge (SOC) indicates how much capacity or energy it still has stored. Nonlinear behaviour, ageing and degradation, temperature effects, high self-discharge, load changes, and a variety of other factors make estimation difficult. To overcome these difficulties in estimation combination of various methods and algorithms are required. The estimation of the initial state of charge is the primary flaw in the coulomb counting approach. For precise state of charge estimation, we proposed an improved version of the enhanced coulomb counting technique. Generic battery of 48V-30AH is designed and considered for evaluation of proposed method. Simulink model is developed considering situational awareness, non-linear characteristics such as driving loads, operational conditions. Measured SOC and modelled SOC are compared, and results show that they are almost similar. In the future work, the estimation accuracy will be improved by adaptive estimation, combining and comparing the similar estimation methods.

articleTitle: Customer Segmentation Using Hierarchical Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: In the dynamic landscape of retail, understanding customer behavior is paramount for businesses seeking to optimize marketing strategies and enhance the shopping experience. This study explores the utilization of hierarchical clustering techniques for mall customer segmentation, with a focus on the paper titled ’MALL CUSTOMER SEGMENTATION USING MACHINE LEARNING’ as the benchmark. Our dataset encompasses a diverse range of mall customers, spanning demographics and behavioral attributes. Hierarchical clustering systematically groups customers into clusters, revealing distinct segments within the mall’s customer base. A comprehensive analysis of these clusters unveils profound insights into customer tendencies, preferences, and purchasing habits. These insights form a solid foundation for tailored marketing campaigns, personalized recommendations, and resource allocation within the mall. The study contributes significantly to customer analytics, providing retailers with a powerful tool to gain a competitive edge in the retail sector. By leveraging hierarchical clustering for mall customer segmentation, businesses can enhance customer satisfaction, drive sales, and foster lasting customer relationships. This paper underscores the importance of data-driven methodologies in understanding customer behavior and offers a practical framework for businesses to harness the potential of hierarchical clustering for strategic decision-making in the retail industry.

articleTitle: Temporal and Spatial Dynamics of Pine Wilt Disease: Insights from a Hybrid CNN-LSTM Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: The current research proposes a novel method of multi-classifying the Pine Wilt Disease severity using the hybrid model that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. The paper aims to address the most critical issue of accurately distinguishing between five levels of disease severity, and it implements CNNs to extract spatial features and LSTMs to process temporal data. Training and testing over a complete dataset consisting of images of pine trees affected by Pine Wilt Disease is rigorously performed to maintain the robustness and accuracy of the model in real-world usage. The methodology involves an extensive image preprocessing phase that includes normalization and augmentation, thereby ensuring that the model is exposed to a large set of disease manifestations. With CNNs for detailed feature extraction and LSTMs for capturing the disease's progression over time as the base, the hybrid model shows a sophisticated understanding of the Pine Wilt Disease severity, while exceeding the traditional diagnostic methods' limits. The evaluation of the model confirms an overall accuracy of 98.13% in the classification of disease severity into the set of five levels, which constitutes a substantial improvement over existing models. This accuracy substantiates the model as a good resource for forest management which in turn will help in efficient monitoring, pest control, and mitigation of Pine Wilt Disease. Moreover, the comparative analysis brings forward the improved ability of the CNN-LSTM hybrid model to take charge of temporal aspects, resulting in a complete solution for the complex classification problem. Thus, not only does this study show the practicability and efficiency of consulting a hybrid deep learning method for plant disease severity classification, but it also provides new prospects for plant pathology and disease management in the future. The results thus go towards the wider domain of agricultural technology giving suggestions that may be used for the detection and classification of different plant diseases and hence favoring sustainable forestry practices and ecosystem preservation.

articleTitle: Precise Measuring of MGNREGA pit works using Image Processing and IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)is an initiative established by the government of India to support the unemployed people in rural areas by providing them alternative employment. MGNREGA plays a vital role in sustainable development of economic, agriculture and forest income. Digging pit is one of the works associated with MGNREGA and its measurements can be measured through tape and ruler which is manual process. Hence the process results in easy manipulation of data and people are not receiving the wages for what they have worked. To overcome these limitations, the project developed an image based IoT application to measure and calculate the pit dimensions and allocate wages to workers. The pit boundaries can be detected by canny edge detection algorithm and depth can be obtained from ultrasonic sensor. Finally, this project developed an android application. This can be beneficiary for the administrators to monitor day to day progress and it results in better resource allocation of lands.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Improved Triple Band Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to design triple-band FIR filters, in which improved finite cosine time functions are used. In this paper, we address a limitation in the recently published paper, wherein the insertion loss of the edge bands was 6 dB higher than that of the central band. The sidelobe decay in the proposed design is improved to 30 dB/octave, compared to 18 dB/octave in the earlier paper. Two FIR filter designs with sampled finite time functions are illustrated.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Microwave Absorbers Based on Biodegradable Agricultural Waste Materials in the X-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: In this paper, agricultural waste materials have been used in the development of microwave absorbers due to their favorable dielectric properties and hence suitable for anechoic chamber applications, stealth structure and electromagnetic devices applications. This paper describes the efficacy of a microwave absorber made from different agriculture waste materials named as rice husk (RH), sugarcane bagasse (SCB), peanut shell (PS) and corn husk (CH). The materials are characterized in terms of their surface morphology and elemental analysis to understand their capability to absorb electromagnetic waves. Likewise, their dielectric properties are evaluated by transmission line method in the X-band frequency range (8.2-12.4 GHz). Furthermore, the designed samples are simulated to evaluate their reflectivity by the use of CST microwave simulator. From the results it can be concluded that the all four types of agricultural residues have the potential to be used as microwave absorbers.

articleTitle: Synchronization Support in 64-bit Out-Of-Order Superscalar Dual-Core RISC-V Processor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: This paper discusses the implementation of atomic instructions in a dual-core 64-bit out-of-order superscalar processors based on the open-source RISC-V instruction set architecture. Leveraging the advantage of RISC-V’s modularization characteristics, each core implements RV64IMAFDC extension and optional supervisor and user mode privilege levels. In this paper, we focus on the A-extension, the atomic instruction set extension. This extension introduces instructions that provide atomic memory operations, enabling synchronization across multiple RISC-V harts within the same memory space. Our goal is to present an efficient execution flow of atomic memory operation instructions and Load-Reserved/Store-Conditional instructions for a dual-core System-on-Chip. We subsequently verify the synchronization capabilities through the execution of a standalone game application on SoC implemented on a Xilinx Kintex UltraScale KU085 FPGA-based board.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of Almost Sub Frame Approach as Inter Cell Interference Management in LTE-A Macro – Pico Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Heterogeneous networks are promising solutions for enhancing network performance of LTE-A mobile networks by deploying small cells within the area of the serving macro cells. The goal of deploying such networks is to offload data from the congested macro cells towards the small cells. However, cross tier interference is a serious issue, which is introduced due to the transmitted power difference between Macro cell node and small cell node. Hence, cell age users are mainly affected by high power interference originated from Macro node. The paper develops enhanced inter-cell interference coordination using Almost Blank Sub-Frame (ABS) to improve user throughput. This can be achieved by stopping data transmission on in certain sub frame of macro cell while Pico users are scheduled at the same frame. Computer simulation results depict that the performance of Pico cell users is highly degraded, especially for cell edge users. The ABS technique improves cell edge user throughput of Pico cell by 95% and center cell user throughput by 75.25%.

articleTitle: Severity Calculation of Tar Disease in Sorghum Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Sorghum, a crucial cereal crop, is confronted with challenges from diseases such as Tar spot, Anthracnose and Rust impacting production. In response to the scarcity of relevant data, our project proposes a Deep Learning solution utilizing the ResNet architecture to classify Tar disease severity in sorghum leaves. Facing the challenge of limited data, we meticulously curated a benchmark dataset comprising healthy and affected sorghum leaves. To enhance our system's intelligence, we selected ResNet, a specialized form of Deep Learning known for understanding intricate leaf patterns and performing well with a small dataset. The proposed methodology incorporates image masking to emphasize disease-related features and severity assessment through automated detection and quantification of black spots. The project aims to deliver a robust and reliable tool for accurately identifying and assessing Tar disease severity in sorghum, providing valuable insights for effective agricultural management.

articleTitle: AI-based Online Proctoring System with YoLo-v3 & MMOD CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: The popularity of remote learning has increased recently. However, there has never been a better alternative for academic exams. Certain colleges have compiled assignments that allow students to simply copy and paste using the internet, although others have adopted remote proctoring, in which an observer uses a manual proctor to keep track of student’s activities. In this paper, we have suggested a method to create an integrated AI-based proctoring system that could help in stopping exam cheating. The technology detects and reports mal practices, and the system is economical and safe.

articleTitle: Quantitative Analysis of Biofield Energy Imbalance Through Color Segmentation and Classification Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Human biofield imaging is a non-invasive, radiation free, preventive, live imaging system capable of diagnosing human ailments at physical, mental, and emotional level and complements current practices of diagnosis. Biofield image shows energy field existing around and within the body. Imbalance in this energy field indicates disharmony in an individual, which appears in biofield image in different shades of red color. As part of the research work conducted, we tried to create a systematic approach to train a machine learning model to detect the severity of imbalance in the biofield energy and classify the biofield images as in three buckets namely less, moderate, and high imbalance of energy. In this experimentation we selected only the images capturing the knee section of person and performed the analysis. The method designed to train and classify the images has shown positive results and is matching with the clinical analysis done by Biofield experts on the same set of data with more than 80% accuracy. This helps to claim to manipulate individual energy fields enhance healing and wellbeing.

articleTitle: An IoT based Pipeline Management and Leakage Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: In this paper an Internet of Things(IoT)-based automated pipeline management and leakage monitoring system is presented. Despite the present global water crisis issues, reducing water use is the only way to prevent the catastrophe of water shortage from growing worse. Smart water sensors are utilized to track the water usage and notify the consumers when leaks are discovered. IoT makes automation and enhancement of safety standards in a pipeline easier. In this paper, an IoT-based water leakage detection method with associated sensor control scheme is proposed and a hardware prototype is developed to show the validity of the proposed water management scheme. It includes smart alerting approaches such as message sending and doing data analytics on sensor readings. By putting the programme into practice, businesses and customers may control their water consumption and system more effectively.

articleTitle: Efficient Credit Card Fraud Detection Based on Multiple ML Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: The occurrence of credit card fraud has become a major worry in the current digital era, impacting financial institutions and customers alike. Effective and reliable fraud detection systems are in high demand as fraudulent actions continue to change. Sophisticated machine learning algorithms have become essential instruments in tackling this problem. The design and assessment of a credit card fraud detection system based on well-known machine learning algorithms— Random Forest, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and XGBoost—is thoroughly investigated in this study.The increasing number of digital transactions has given criminals additional chances to take advantage of holes in payment systems. As a result, the requirement for proactive and flexible fraud detection systems has increased significantly. In order to solve this urgent issue, this study investigates how well machine learning algorithms can detect fraudulent credit card transactions.The machine learning algorithms that are the subject of this study were selected due to their demonstrated efficacy in a number of fields, including the identification of credit card fraud. The models Random Forest, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and XGBoost are highly respected for their capacity to accurately predict complex patterns. A variety of real and fraudulent credit card transaction datasets are used to develop each method and evaluate its performance in a controlled setting.

articleTitle: An Experimental Analysis of RL based Compiler Optimization Techniques using Compiler GYM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: Compiler optimization significantly impacts algorithm performance, whether it may be graph-based, parallel computing workloads and more. Understanding how these algorithms' performance varies under different optimization scenarios is crucial. This study explores diverse Reinforcement Learning (RL) algorithms for code optimization in Compiler Gym, including Actor-Critic, Random Walk, Tabular Q, and a Brute Force approach. Three benchmark datasets, Dijkstra, CRC32, and npbv0 from Compiler Gym libraries, and are evaluated using execution time and maximum reward metrics. This study reveals that the npbv0 dataset consistently outperforms others across all RL algorithms, demonstrating its compatibility with RL-based compiler optimization. This research highlights the role of compiler optimization in algorithm performance, emphasizing the potential of RL techniques in diverse workloads, with npbv0 excelling as a benchmark dataset.

articleTitle: Decoding ERP Training for Non-Technical Users: A Novel Algorithm-Driven Framework for Enhanced Training Effectiveness
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: This research studies Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) training for non-technical employees by integrating Machine Learning techniques, specifically Decision Tree algorithm, into the training analysis process. The research methodology comprises a dual approach: a qualitative analysis of 20 key ERP training articles and the application of Decision Tree algorithms for data categorization and prediction. This innovative method allows for an examination of training methodologies and effectiveness. Key findings from the literature underscore the necessity for user-friendly training approaches, particularly for non-technical stakeholders grappling with complex ERP systems. These findings informed the development of a novel training framework, which includes components like simplified system integration, gamified training modules, and AI-powered interactive support. This framework is designed to address common challenges faced by non-technical users, such as difficulties with system integration and the need for ongoing post-training support. A significant contribution of this study is the introduction of a novel algorithm to quantify training effectiveness. This algorithm represents a leap in evaluating ERP training approaches, moving from subjective assessments to a more structured, data-driven evaluation. It systematically assesses the impact of various training components, grounded in empirical evidence from the literature. The study not only contributes to academic research but also provides practical strategies for organizations to optimize ERP system utilization, ensuring comprehensive training for all users.

articleTitle: Development of Internal Inverter Controller System with PWM VSC based STATCOM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: The various internal inverter controller schemes have been implemented to enhance performance of the Statcom. The continuous development in the controller schemes increases complications in the controlling. The importance of the DC capacitor and voltage control methods are compared and contrasted. To achieve spectacular overall performance, the control system incorporates synchronization, generation of gate trigger pulses for switching devices, and phase shifting of VSC output using a microcontroller. The paper addresses critical challenges related to the development of a VAR compensator internal inverter controller design. The device's topology includes a voltage source converter (VSC) and an IGBT. SPWM is a technique for controlling the converter output voltage (phase and amplitude). The results of using VSC inversion and phase shift to regulate reactive power. This demonstrates the prototype's exceptional performance and agility in development.

articleTitle: Modeling GPP with Machine Learning using Multisource Features based on Fluxnet Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 9th International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
abstract: One of the most crucial markers for forecasting the future trend of climate change and for adopting sustainable development plans is the understanding of the carbon that plants absorbs from the atmosphere. Terrestrial Gross Primary Productivity (GPP), a measure of carbon uptake, is the total amount of carbon that is assimilated by photosynthesis in a terrestrial ecosystem. Eddy covariance measurements taken from Flux-towers are regarded as accurate GPP estimates. However, building a tower is expensive and difficult to maintain, thus we only have a small number of towers for flux measurements. Because satellite data have a greater resolution and continuous coverage, we can use them create models to estimate GPP at larger geographical and temporal scales.
